steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Place the ground beef into a skillet over medium heat, and brown the meat, breaking it apart into crumbles as it cooks, about 8 minutes. Drain excess fat. Stir in the taco seasoning, water, chili powder, cooked rice, salt, garlic salt, black pepper, and 1 can of tomato sauce; mix until thoroughly combined. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the bell peppers in half lengthwise, and remove stems, membranes, cores, and seeds. Place a steamer insert into a large saucepan, and fill with water to just below the bottom of the steamer. Cover, and bring the water to a boil over high heat. Place the peppers into the steamer insert, cover the pan, and steam until just tender, 3 to 5 minutes.

Place the steamed peppers into the prepared baking dish, and fill lightly with the meat filling. Press 1 cube of Colby-Jack cheese into the center of the filling in each pepper, and spoon the remaining can of tomato sauce over the peppers. Cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until the peppers are tender and the filling is hot, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Stuffed Mexican Peppers
raw_recipe.description: Mexican-inspired ground beef and rice stuffing fills red or green bell peppers for a family-pleasing meal.

video.description: Easy stuffed peppers full of spice and melted cheese! Ground beef and taco seasoning fill the bowls of hallowed out peppers. A cube of cheese melts into gooey deliciousness after baking. Enjoy with a side of chips!

review.reviewBody: I made these as is with the exception that I used poblano peppers instead of bell. Why? Well hubby does not care for bells and well poblanas just seemed right. I roasted them in the oven beforehand, let them cool, and removed most of their skin and they were mmm mmm good. I think I will add black beans or corn the next time I make them and also sub the colby jack ( I used a colby blend this go around because that is all my store carried) for cheddar or mexiblend. As written I give these a 4 but with the sub of poblanos I give it a 5 all the way. Thanks for sharing Jasgirl!

I adapted this recipe and cooked it in the Crock-Pot for 4 hours. I used a liner for the Crock-Pot, and added a 15-ounce can of tomato sauce and a 15-ounce can of bruschetta tomatoes to the Crock-Pot. For the meat mixture, in addition to the ingredients listed, I added a Vidalia onion, 1 can of niblet corn, 5 mini red, yellow and orange peppers, an egg, a sprinkle of breadcrumbs and substituted milk (for the water) to make my mixture. (Instead of sprinkling the dry taco seasoning into the meat, I blended the taco seasoning with the milk. Yes, it didn't all completely dissolve in the milk, but when it was mixed into the other ingredients, it blended perfectly.) I then stuffed the mixture into 3 green bell peppers. Extra meat mixture was rolled into mini meatballs and added to the sauce. I cooked this for 4 hours and added one can of DRAINED black beans during the last hour of cooking. This turned out phenomenal, incredible flavor and texture and clean-up was so easy. For this meal, I did not need any other sides because of the rice, beans, peppers, corn and tomatoes.

I made these and changed this recipe up becuase I wanted more of a Mexican flavor. I used 1 pound ground beef, 1/2 chopped white onion, 1 tablespoon Spanish Gardens taco seasoning, 1 can original Rotel, 1/2 cup cooked rice (I cooked the rice in chicken stock for more flavor), a couple pinches of salt (the taco seasoning I used does NOT have added salt, so this needed some salt), 1 heaping teaspoon of minced garlic, serveral shakes of ground black pepper, 4 poblano peppers, and shredded Cobly jack cheese. I cut the Poblanos in half length-wise, deseeded, and roasted them in the oven on 400 for 15 minutes. I browned the beef with the onion, salt and pepper and drained the grease. I added the garlic, taco seasoning, rotel, and let it simmer about 10 minutes while the rice cooked. Then I added the cooked rice. I spooned the ground beef and rice mixture into the Poblano peppers and sprinkled the shredded cheese on top. I popped them back in the 400 degree oven for about 15 minutes (until the cheese was nicely melted). I served them with sour cream. These were fantastic! Great starter recipe you can make tweaks to for your own taste!

Wonderful recipe! I did have to make some changes as I was out of several things. I didn’t have fresh tomatoes so I used a can of petite diced tomatoes. Didn’t have tomato sauce so I used 1 can of original Rotel, used ground turkey instead of hamburger, didn’t have enough taco seasoning so I added an extra tsp of chili powder and added 1 can of corn. After cooking the meat and rice (the rice made 1.5 cups), I added everything in the same cast iron skillet for the recommended 20 minutes. I did the steps exactly as per the recipe. They were so delicious! I had tons of filling left over so I added a can of refried beans to it and used it the next day in burritos. The mix got spicier overnight and the burritos were superb. 

Hopefully next time I make this I’ll have the correct ingredients.

Keep it simple microwave peppers 4 minutes add a cup of rice a cup of water a can of rotel tomatoes not drained taco seasoning garlic and chili powder.. add tomato sauce on top and Mexican cheese cover 20 minutes uncover 5 .. will fill at least 4 peppers. Follow directions re simmer time and bake time.

Pretty good with additional flavors for us. Broiled the peppers till lightly browned before stuffing and used a meat alternative with added jalapeno, garlic, cumin, oregano, cilantro, double the taco seasoning and onion. I used canned tomato with green chilies and some broth to simmer the mix for a bit till thick. Basically, anything you like in a taco. Used mozzarella, for the inside, cheddar on top halfway through baking. Also used cauliflower (riced) vs rice for lower carb. Served with sour cream, guacamole, salsa....will do again

Delicious! I made my own taco seasoning and didn't pre-steam the peppers since I like a little crunch. I did add a splash or two of beef broth to the baking dish to help steam them, while cooking and for a little extra flavour. I had to sub the tomato sauce with a can of tomato paste and equal amount of water. I missed the 3/4 cup of water in the recipe for some reason but found the consistency great as it was. Served with a little extra cheese for sprinkling and some sour cream. Next time, I think I'll try using salsa for the tomato sauce for even more zing. Thanks for a great, easy and delicious recipe!

OMG SOOOOOOOOO Good!!! The only thing i did different was bake the bell peppers at 375 for 20 minutes cause i didn't have a steamer and i did that while the meat mixture simmered for its 20 minutes. when i filled i did the cube in cheddar cheese in the middle and did slices of pepper jack cheese on top! the meat mixture was wonderful!

also I just dumped a 16 oz can of tomato sauce in with the rice and meat. i didnt pour it on top (i missed that part in the instructions, but it turned out good!)

Best stuffed peppers I’ve have so far. However, I did make a few adjustments for my family’s taste... (adjustments)-Add ground Italian sausage, onions & garlic to beef. Season beef/sausage mixture (add rosemary/oregano/sazon/adobo). Add Rotel diced tomatoes w/chiles. Add some cheese cubes to meat mix while simmering (stir when melted). Serve with green salad and fresh garlic Tuscan bread. YUMMY

I made it with taco seasoned ground turkey. I also added chopped onions and cumin. Only add salt to taste as it may be too salty for some. I used reduced fat sharp cheddar cheese in the bottom before the meat and on top as well. I added sliced olives. Over all delicious with these additions.

A few minor changes:
1. Swapped beef broth for the water
2. Added some left over Rotlel tomatoes to mixture
3. Swapped cayenne for red pepper flakes, to taste, no specific amount
4. Used shredded 4 oz. Monterey Jack cheese with jalapenos, 1/4 in mixture,
1/2 on top of mixture in peppers, 1/4 on top of tomatoes sauce.
No changes it is a family favorite

This was good, but I like what I make better. I prep whole medium size green bell peppers, by cutting the tops off, cleaning out the seeds, etc under running cold water. I then boil them whole in salted water until fork tender still able to stand up in a baking pan. In the mean time I remove Chorizo sausage from the casing. I use 1 sausage per pepper. Cook the sausage with some diced onion, and diced pepper from the tops, When fully cooked, drain and place the sausage mixture in a large bowl, add a small handful of Mex blend cheese, 1 egg, seasoned breadcrumbs and make a filling using some canned Enchelada sauce for moisture if necessary. I use the 'mild' ench sauce. But feel free to experiment using medium or even hot. I fill the pre-cooked peppers loosely.. pour more ench sauce over each pepper. Cover and bake until warmed through. Uncover, top each pepper with Mex blend cheese and continue baking until melted. The hub likes this served with yellow rice on the side. If you prefer, you can add cooked yellow rice to the filling...or even a boxed Mexican rice mix.

This recipe was a crowd pleaser! Definitely have to steam the peppers before for a perfect bite. Some alterations: - We added half a can of black beans and substituted one can of tomato sauce with tomatoes and green chilies. I was able to fill four large bell peppers. - Rather than taco seasoning we just did 2 teaspoons of Cumin, Chili Powder & Salt plus 1 teaspoon of garlic powder & pepper. Came out delicious!

I have made this several times. I like to add a can of diced tomatoes with green chilis and some corn kernels. Black beans would be good but my husband won't eat them. I get my peppers ready and then steam them in the microwave for a few minutes. Will definitely make this again.

My family loves these - even the grandkids. They aren't too spicy because I use both tomato sauce and Rotel mild sauce for the topping. I also use sharp cheddar cheese in the middle. The peppers with a small green salad is all you need for a complete meal. And I never have left overs.

I make these peppers often. My family enjoys the Mexican twist on stuffed peppers. Instead of rice I use a can of drained and rinsed black beans. I also use Cabot Pepper Jack Cheese to add a little more heat. This recipe is wonderful!
We cooked the rice in with the meat and simmer it all together
